name: Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B

lineage.base_model: Ornith-1.0-35B-A3B, itself built on Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 (the base of 1.5 is not stated; parameter count equals Qwen3.6-35B-A3B)
lineage.how_derived: continued pretraining, mid-training, post-training with reinforcement learning in a self-improvement loop (task generation, scaffold construction, rollouts)

purpose: The builder presents it as a step toward foundation models built through end-to-end self-improvement; the intended users are developers building agents and terminal-based coding tools (tool calling, OpenCode and similar CLIs). It claims to beat Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-31B on coding and agentic benchmarks with 3 B active parameters.

Rust.evidence: our eval: 8/22 within 4 attempts on llama.cpp (Q4_K_M), 4/12 on Tona (stopped at 12); the Coder solves 2/22; third party MultiPL-E Rust 0.75 for the base (single-function problems, much easier)

Go.evidence: first measurement is partial: 7 of the first 9 exercises within 4 attempts on llama.cpp, stopped at 9/39, no verdict

JavaScript.evidence: third party MultiPL-E 0.90 on the base model (ManniX-ITA CoderX card)

license.name: MIT (declared by the publisher on the model card, in the GGUF metadata and in its GitHub repository; the LICENSE file is missing in the Hugging Face repositories)
license.notes: Publisher declares MIT in four places (research/2026-11-25-ornith-license.md): card YAML license: mit with a dead license_link, GGUF general.license = mit, and https://github.com/ornith-ai/Ornith-1 with a full MIT LICENSE whose README says both generations (1.0 and 1.5) are MIT licensed. No HF repo of ornith-ai ships a LICENSE file (rechecked 2026-11-25). The publisher names Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 as base for 1.0 only; config.json shows the Qwen3.5-MoE architecture; those bases are Apache-2.0 and their attribution is not carried by Ornith. verified stays false: the text was read in the code repository, not next to the model files. Recheck before every release whether the file appeared on Hugging Face.

architecture.kind: hybrid Gated DeltaNet + gated attention MoE
architecture.attention: 30 Gated DeltaNet + 10 gated full attention layers (16 Q / 2 KV heads, head dim 256)
architecture.why_this_design: The card states no architecture reasons. It describes the training goal: end-to-end self-improvement that jointly optimizes task generation, scaffold construction and solution rollouts instead of fixed human-curated tasks and harnesses. Ornith-1.0 was built on Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 with continued pre-training, mid-training and post-training.

strengths: Strongest coding agent numbers per active parameter among the small MoE models (vendor), SWE-bench Verified 79
Rust: 8/22 against the Coder's 2/22 in our paired eval (p = 0.031, with a favourable sampler)
Fits every class from 12 GB VRAM upward at Q4_K_M; very high decode on Tona (median 113 tok/s)
No sign of a dropped language in the base model
weaknesses: Behind the Coder on long agentic tasks per vendor table (DeepSWE 22, Toolathlon 48.7 against the Flash-Next base 58.7 and 73.5)
Numbers are vendor only; vendor is new
Verbose chain of thought on simple tasks (HF discussion 5)
Q4_K_M quality unmeasured; license file missing
soft.behavior: Reasoning model with think blocks by default; recommended sampling 0.6/0.95/20 for general use and 1.0 to reproduce the benchmarks. Plain fenced code blocks instead of FILE headers in our harness smoke test. Tona's chat template renderer for it matches the GGUF Jinja template byte for byte on 9 of 9 cases.
best_for: Rust and general coding agents on 12 to 16 GB VRAM
avoid_for: single-file visual HTML generation was reported broken by one user (anecdote)

user_reports.summary: 'Not for coding?': single-file HTML aquarium with runtime errors at Q8, v1.5 worse than 1.0 and Qwen 27B; replies suggest Q6 and checking sampling
Excessive chain of thought on simple tasks

Launch complaints: file read/write tool calls failing and endless thinking in a Pi agent; replies trace most of it to speculative decoding and KV-cache quantization (Q4 cache), and the shipped mtp.* tensors looked untrained
Constant looping reported; advice: switch thinking off and use 8-bit weights
mtp.* tensors look like random initialisation (std exactly 0.02); a community-trained MTP head reaches 69 % code acceptance against 37 % for the shipped head (fixed shard re-uploaded 2026-08-23)
RTX 5090, llama.cpp Q4_K_M: 271 tok/s decode and 673 tok/s at 8 concurrent requests, compared with Gemma 4-26B-A4B and Qwen3.8-27B
MMLU-style knowledge benchmark trade-off: lower general knowledge than Qwen at the same quant (oQ4e); defenders note the model targets agentic coding

soft.maturity: New vendor (Ornith 1.0 earlier in 2026); 26 open discussions on the GGUF repo; large community requant ecosystem (221 quantizations, 40 finetunes listed).

tona_fit.reason: Runs on Tona (decode, MTP, kernel prefill) and is the best measured Rust option so far; Go still undecided. Agent quality on long tasks must be shown by one full agent eval on the finished implementation before it is offered.
blockers: Go not measured to the end
no full agent eval on Tona yet
